html:
SMTO-CMP-0025 — The AI tried to finish while work was still in progress

GUID: 59f520ad-7e2f-4d40-a3a0-77179fdbe03c
Slug: completion-pending-work
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI tried to finish, but something in this task is still running or waiting, such as a command, an approval or a question for you. SMTO didn't mark the task done, and nothing was cancelled.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task and look for steps marked Running, Needs approval or Needs input. These are the things the AI tried to finish ahead of.
  2. Answer any question or approval request SMTO shows. For a step that is still running, wait until it shows Completed or Failed. SMTO only accepts a finish once nothing in the task is left waiting or running.
  3. If the task stopped as Partial · resumable, check which steps are done, then select Resume or send a message asking SMTO to finish. Checking first means you won't ask for a change that already happened.

What success looks like

  • No step shows Running, Needs approval or Needs input, and the task ends as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start a running command again; let it finish, or stop the task with Stop first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because the run still has pending work: a pending operation, an open user or approval wait, a running/pending/starting job, or unfinished task-board items.

What this means

  • Terminal normalization/direct completion finds pending operations, waits, approvals, active jobs or unfinished task-board items. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Terminal normalization/direct completion finds pending operations, waits, approvals, active jobs or unfinished task-board items.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact pending owner and current state before making a whole-task completion claim.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run state's pending, pending_wait, approval_pending, jobs and task_board.tasks to find the exact owner of the unfinished work. Settle each through its supported control (answer or approve the wait, let the job finish or manage it, complete or cancel the task-board item) before completion is declared again; do not relaunch work that is still running.
  • Finish or explicitly resolve pending operations before claiming the whole task completed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Required pending work resolves through its supported controls and original receipts remain intact.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
